results.title: Tax card and tax counseling - International House Helsinki
results.text:
# Tax card and tax counseling

If you are in Finland working and receiving pay, or if you are an entrepreneur, you will need a Finnish tax card. You will also need a tax card if you receive taxable benefits opens in new tab from from the Social Insurance Institution of Finland (Kela).

You can apply for a tax card by visiting the Finnish Tax Administration (Vero) at International House Helsinki (IHH). Vero can also provide you with information about taxation in Finland for individuals.

### Vero

The Finnish Tax Administration (Vero) is the agency that issues tax cards and manages taxation in Finland.

You can apply for a tax card by visiting Vero’s service desk at International House Helsinki (IHH).

- How to visit Vero at IHH
- Vero – Arriving in Finland from overseas

The recommended way to get a tax card depends on whether you have a Finnish personal identity code.

Apply for a personal identity code at IHH

You can also receive a personal identity code for tax purposes by visiting Vero’s service desk.

## How to visit Vero at IHH

If you already have a Finnish personal identity code

If you already have a Finnish personal identity code but do not yet have a tax card, you can get one by calling the Tax Administration’s Tax Card Service at +358 29 497 050 (Mon–Fri, 9–12). You can also apply for a tax card in person at a Tax Administration’s service desk. Please note that appointments cannot be booked for tax card matters.

If you don’t yet have a Finnish personal identity code

If you don’t yet have a Finnish personal identity code and need a tax card, you must visit a Tax Administration’s service desk to register and get a Finnish personal identity code and a tax card. You can call the Tax Administration’s telephone service at +358 29 497 010 (Mon–Fri, 9–16) to book an appointment to get a Finnish personal identity code and a tax card at the same time.

The Tax Administration (Vero) serves customers on weekdays from 9:00 to 16:00.

Before visiting Vero, make sure you have all the necessary documents completed and with you. Please bring the following documents:

- A valid passport or identity card
- An employment contract
- A filled-in application form (see below)
- An estimation of your total annual income including wage income and possible fringe benefits, holiday pay, bonuses etc.

Choose the relevant application below and fill it for your visit. The forms are also available at IHH.

- ### Application form if you are arriving to stay for more than six months in Finland

- Application for tax card, tax prepayment or tax number – current or former foreign residents (Form 5042e)
- ### Application form if you are staying for six months or less in Finland

- Non-resident’s application for tax at source card, tax card, tax prepayment or tax number (Form 5057e)

You can visit Vero’s service desk at IHH without an appointment.

## Contact

- ## Contact Vero at IHH

You do not need an appointment to visit the Finnish Tax Administration (Vero) at International House Helsinki.

### Opening hours

- Monday - Friday 09.00 – 16.00 

## Questions

 I am about to start work in construction. Can I apply for a tax number at International House Helsinki? 

If you work in construction, you need a tax number (veronumero) and a tax card. You can apply for both at the Vero’s service desk. The service is available both by appointment and as a walk-in service. Bring along your employment contract as well as a valid passport or identity.

 How long does it take to get a tax card? 

You usually get a tax card right away when you visit the Vero service desk, if you have a Finnish Personal Identity Code and required information about your income. More information about tax cards

 Now that I have my tax card what should I do with it? 

Your employer needs it to pay your salary and to make a withholding of the right amount. Please ask your employer for instructions on where and how to deliver your tax card for the payroll. If you do not provide your tax card, your employer must withhold 60 percent of your salary.

 I have moved to Helsinki due to my partner's work. Do I also need a tax card? 

You need a tax card only if you have taxable income. In case you are currently not working, you don’t necessarily need a tax card. Please note that if you work for a foreign employer while living in Finland, under certain circumstances, you will have to pay your taxes in Finland. It is also noteworthy that some social benefits are subject to tax. In case you receive e.g. unemployment benefit, please deliver an appropriate tax card to Kela or other payer of the benefit.

 I have a tax card. Is that sufficient proof of my right to work in Finland? 

No. Nor does for example a Finnish personal identity code, identification card or driving license prove right to work. If you are a citizen of a non-EU/EEA country, your right to work need to be checked from your residence permit. In case of a citizen of an EU/EEA or Nordic country, right to work can be proved by a passport.

It is also worth noting that EU citizens must register their right of residence if their stay in Finland lasts more than 3 months.

 What is a pre-completed tax return? 

Every year in March or April, you will receive your pre-completed tax return in MyTax and by post. This includes information the tax administration has about your income and assets for the previous year. Check your tax return and make the necessary corrections and additions by the stated deadline. If all the information is correct, you do not need to do anything. Your tax return also states if you can expect a tax refund or if you have to pay back taxes.

 Can I get a Finnish personal identity code from the Finnish Tax Administration? 

You can request a personal identity code from:

- The Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV)
- The Finnish Tax Administration (Vero), if you need a personal identity code for tax purposes, such as for a tax card.
- The Finnish Immigration Service (Migri), when you are granted a residence permit, a residence card, or when your right of residence is registered.

Ratapihantie 7, 00520 Helsinki

results.text:
Remember these when you start working in Finland - Work in Finland - Suomi.fi

# Remember these when you start working in Finland

## Prove to your employer that your residence permit includes a right to work

Show your residence permit to your employer. They usually take a copy of it.

### Do I need to give my passport and residence permit to my employer for safekeeping?

No. Show your passport or residence permit to your employer when they need it for example to verify your right to work. However, always ask the original documents to be returned to you.

### Where can I find additional information about proving my right to work?

- Read about the right to work in more detail on the website of the Finnish Immigration Service Opens in a new window..
- Read about proving your right to work in more detail on the website of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration in Finland Opens in a new window..

Updated: 27/6/2022

## Prove to your employer that you have an EU citizens’ right to work

Show your passport or other official travel document to your employer. They usually take a copy of it.

As an EU or EEA citizen, you have an unrestricted right to work in Finland even if you have not yet received a decision on your application for EU registration.

### Do I need to give my passport or official travel document to my employer for safekeeping?

No. Show your passport or identity card to your employer when they need it for example to verify your right to work. However, always ask the original documents to be returned to you.

### Where can I find additional information about proving my right to work?

- Read about the right to work in more detail on the website of the Finnish Immigration Service. Opens in a new window.
- Read about proving your right to work in more detail on the website of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration in Finland. Opens in a new window.

Updated: 26/7/2022

## Familiarise yourself with the rights, obligations, and practices associated with work

Find out what rights and obligations you have when working in Finland. For example, you have a right to receive pay according to a collective agreement and an obligation to do your work carefully.

For more information about Finnish working life in several languages, see

- InfoFinland website Opens in a new window.
- As a foreign employee in Finland guide (tyosuojelu.fi) Opens in a new window.
- Workers’ rights in Finland webinar (tyosuojelu.fi) Opens in a new window..

You can also download the free Work Help Finland mobile application Opens in a new window. to your smartphone. The content of the application has been translated into 26 languages, so you can access the information about your rights and responsibilities as an employee in Finland in your native language.

Get to know the customs and practices that your own workplace has. You can ask for help and advice from your supervisor, the HR representative at your workplace, and your colleagues.

Updated: 1/7/2026

## Where do I pay taxes as a posted worker if my stay in Finland is less than 6 months?

You do not usually pay taxes to Finland when

- you are a posted worker
- you stay in Finland for less than 6 months.

There are a few exceptions:

- your foreign employer has a permanent establishment in Finland 
- you are a leased employee
- you are a performing artist

Read more about paying taxes to Finland on the Finnish Tax Administration’s website Opens in a new window..

Even if you do not pay taxes to Finland from your salary, in certain cases you may have to pay social insurance contributions to Finland. The contributions will be deducted directly from your salary.

### When do I have to pay compulsory social insurance contributions to Finland?

If you come from an EU or EEA country, Switzerland or the United Kingdom, you will pay social insurance contributions to Finland if you do not have an A1 certificate.

Finland's statutory social insurance contributions are earnings-related pension contributions, insurance for accidents at work and occupational diseases, unemployment insurance contributions and health insurance payments.

If you come to Finland as a posted employee from other countries than 

- an EU or EEA country
- Switzerland 
- Great Britain or
- a country that has entered into a social security agreement with Finland

you do not need to pay earnings-related pension insurance contributions to Finland. You usually need to pay other statutory social security insurance payments to Finland.

Countries that have entered into a social security agreement with Finland are the United States, Canada and Quebec, Australia, Chile, China, India, South Korea, Japan, and Israel.

You can find out your social insurance contributions in the online service of the Finnish Centre for Pensions Opens in a new window..

Updated: 8/1/2024

## Where do I pay taxes when my stay in Finland is over 6 months and I have a foreign employer?

If you live in Finland for more than six months, you will in most cases pay tax to Finland on all your income.

If you make a temporary trip to your home country for example for a vacation, the 6-month period will not be interrupted.

Additional information and instructions on how to pay taxes Opens in a new window..

In certain cases, you may also have to pay social insurance contributions to Finland. The contributions will be deducted directly from your salary.

### When do I have to pay compulsory social insurance contributions to Finland?

If you come from an EU or EEA country, Switzerland or the United Kingdom, you will pay social insurance contributions to Finland if you do not have an A1 certificate.

If you come to Finland as a posted employee for a maximum of two years from a country other than 

- an EU or EEA country 
- Switzerland
- the United Kingdom or 
- a country that has entered into a social security agreement with Finland, 

you do not need to pay earnings-related pension insurance contributions to Finland. You usually need to pay other statutory social security insurance payments to Finland.

Countries that have entered into a social security agreement with Finland are the United States, Canada and Quebec, Australia, Chile, China, India, South Korea, Japan, and Israel.

You can find out your social insurance contributions in the online service of the Finnish Centre for Pensions Opens in a new window..

Additional information about social insurance contributions in Finland (Finnish Centre for Pensions) Opens in a new window..

Updated: 20/6/2023

## A short stay in Finland affects taxation

When you stay in Finland for a maximum of 6 months, you are a person with limited tax liability. This means that you will usually have to pay tax at source from income you receive from Finland. Tax at source is usually 35%. 

Apply for a tax-at-source card and give it to your employer. 

Additional information and instructions on how to pay taxes Opens in a new window..

Updated: 27/6/2022

## You need to pay taxes to Finland when you are staying in the country for more than six months

When you stay in Finland for more than 6 months, you are generally liable to pay taxes. This means that you will usually have to pay tax to Finland from all your income.

The tax rate for your salary is progressively determined on the basis of your income for the entire year. You will need a Finnish personal identity code and a tax card.

Additional information and instructions on how to pay taxes Opens in a new window..

Updated: 27/6/2022

## Apply for a tax card before payment of salary

Follow these steps:

1. Apply for a tax card using the MyTax online service Opens in a new window., from the tax office or by calling a service number. Take your residence permit with you if you are not a citizen of an EU Member State, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, or Switzerland. If you do not yet have a personal identity code, you can obtain it from the tax office.
2. Give the tax card to your employer. Your employer will pay your income tax in accordance with the tax card when they pay your salary.

Read more about the taxation of a foreign employee coming to work in Finland on the website of the Tax Administration Opens in a new window..

Read more about taxation in Ukrainian on the website of the Tax Administration Opens in a new window..

### Can I use the online service?

You can only use the MyTax online service Opens in a new window. when you are able to use strong electronic identification. Strong identification requires, for example, Finnish online banking ID codes or a mobile certificate. You can obtain online banking codes if you are a customer of a Finnish bank, and a mobile certificate if you are a customer of a Finnish telecommunications operator.

You can identify yourself in MyTax service also with

- the identification tokens of the countries that have been approved for cross-border identification in Europe
- the Finnish Authenticator application which is intended for identification only for those foreigners who cannot use common European identification methods.

### Can I start working before I have a tax card?

Your employer needs your tax card in order to pay you a salary. You can usually start working even if you do not have a tax card yet.

An exception to this are construction and shipyard workers who need to have a tax number already before starting work.

### Why do I need to submit my tax card to my employer?

Your employer will check your tax card to see how much tax should be withheld from your salary. If the employer does not have your tax card, 60% of your salary will be withheld as an advance tax.

Updated: 22/4/2025

## Pay attention to these when you receive a salary

- The employer will primarily pay your salary to your bank account. The account can be either Finnish or foreign.
- Check that the pay slip information is in order.
- You should also check the salary information annually in your tax return.

### Do I need a bank account to get paid?

It is good to have a bank account, but it is not necessary for working. The salary will primarily be paid to a bank account. If this is not possible, it can also be paid in cash. In this case, it is important that both the employee and the employer sign an acknowledgement that the salary has been given and received.

### What is a pay slip?

Your employer will provide you with a pay slip at regular intervals. It provides you with detailed information about your salary such as the amount of salary, the amount of tax withheld, the social insurance contributions deducted from your salary, and the pay period. If you receive an hourly rate, also check that the actual number of hours worked is the same as the number of hours displayed in the pay slip.

### Why is the salary I receive on my account lower than the gross salary shown in the pay slip?

The employer will deduct tax compulsory social security contributions from your gross salary and pay them to the authorities. The net salary shown on your pay slip shows how much money you will receive on your account.

### What should I do if I notice a mistake in the pay slip?

Contact your employer's payroll clerk to check the matter. If the matter cannot be resolved, you can ask for help, for example, from your trade union.

### How is the salary information in the tax return checked?

Early in the year the Tax Administration will always send you a pre-completed tax return either on paper or electronically to the MyTax service. Check that the information related to your salary are correct in the tax return. If you notice an error, correct it in the tax return. Also report the error to your employer.

### What should I do if I want to send part of my salary to my home country?

The practices vary depending on many things, such as what your home country is. In some cases, the matter may be handled through your Finnish bank. Another option is to use an online money transfer service of your choice. Sending money is usually subject to a fee, but the amount of the fee may vary greatly depending on the method of transfer and your home country.

Updated: 30/8/2022

## If you wish, you can join a trade union and an unemployment fund

Everyone has the right to join a trade union and an unemployment fund:

- The trade union will help you if problems such as disagreements about the salary or the terms and conditions of work arise between you and your employer. The trade union can also provide you with other support at different stages of your career.
- The unemployment fund may pay earnings-related unemployment benefit if you become unemployed.

### Who will know about my trade union membership?

Trade union membership is not public information. There is no need to inform the employer or anyone else about the membership of the union. The employer will be informed of the membership if the employee requests the employer to deduct for the membership fee directly from the salary. You can also pay the membership fee yourself.

### Which trade union can I join?

The members of the same trade union are usually people who work in the same sector or who have got the same education. For example, employees in the service sector, such as restaurant workers and hotel workers, have their own trade union. 

If you would like to join a trade union, find out what is the trade union for your sector and contact it:

- Affiliated unions of the Confederation of Unions for Professional and Managerial Staff in Finland Opens in a new window.. 
- Affiliated unions of the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions Opens in a new window..
- Trade unions under the Finnish Confederation of Professionals STTK Opens in a new window..

### Which unemployment fund can I join?

You can join the unemployment fund when you join the trade union. You can also join only the unemployment fund. You will find the contact details of the unemployment funds on the website of the Federation of Unemployment Funds in Finland (TYJ) Opens in a new window..

### Why would it be a good idea for me to join a trade union?

The trade union promotes the rights of employees. It also organises training and leisure-time activities to its members. In addition, it provides help and advice if you face a difficult situation in working life. 

The trade union takes part in the negotiations concerning the collective agreements of your sector. The terms and conditions of work for the sector, such as the minimum wages and the working hours, are determined in the collective agreement. Trade unions also take part in the preparation of different laws and regulations related to working life. As a member of the union, you can contribute to what kind of matters your union promotes in different negotiations.

You will find more information about trade unions on the InfoFinland website. Opens in a new window.

### Why should I join an unemployment fund?

The unemployment fund may pay earnings-related unemployment benefit if you become unemployed. If you are not a member of an unemployment fund, you will receive the unemployment benefit paid by Kela if you become unemployed. The earnings-related unemployment allowance is more than the unemployment benefit paid by Kela.

### Does it cost something to be a member of a trade union and an unemployment fund?

The members of a trade union pay a membership fee to the union and, in return, trade unions promote the rights of workers in the sector and offer them various services and benefits. 

The membership fee may be a specific sum or it may be defined as a percentage from the salary, such as 1–2 percent of your salary. Usually, the trade union membership fee also includes the membership fee of the unemployment fund.

As a member of an unemployment fund, you pay a fee that is used to finance unemployment benefits and the administrative costs of the fund. The membership fee of the unemployment fund is less than that of the trade union. You will find the membership fees of the unemployment funds on the website of the Federation of Unemployment Funds in Finland (TYJ) Opens in a new window..

Updated: 18/2/2026

The MyTax e-service is down until Sunday 15 November 6 pm due to a system upgrade. We apologise for any inconvenience. Read more about the service outage

# Work in Finland

Read instructions for arriving in Finland to work here: you need a tax card and/or an individual tax number. To apply for the card and the number, you need a Finnish personal identity code.

Please take into account that service points may not be able to give you a tax card and/or a tax number immediately. The processing time, on the condition that all your information and documents are made available to the Tax Administration, is normally from 1 to 3 business days.

If the tax issue at hand makes it necessary for you to come to the service point, an appointment will be booked for you. We give service – at the service point and by telephone – in Finnish, Swedish and English. If you cannot communicate in Finnish, Swedish or English, bring your own interpreter with you to the service point or call an interpreter during your visit. 

When you come to Finland to work, your tax treatment depends on the length of your stay. The treatment also depends on the country of the employer, i.e. whether you work for a Finnish employer or for a foreign one. Additionally, special tax rules apply to certain professions and types of work.

## A Finnish personal ID 

The Digital and Population Data Services Agency issues Finnish personal IDs. In some cases, IDs can be issued by the Finnish Immigration Service or the Finnish Tax Administration. 

## Instructions for occupational groups 

The income of people in certain occupations – construction workers, seasonal employees, and others – is subject to special tax rules.

## Coming to work for a Finnish employer 

Read instructions for arriving in Finland to work for a Finnish employer.

## Work for a foreign employer 

Read instructions for arriving in Finland to work for a foreign employer.

## The tax number 

If you are working at a construction site or on an installation project or at a shipyard you must have a tax number. See the instructions on how to apply for a tax number and how to enter it into the tax number register.

## Temporary protection to persons fleeing Ukraine 

You can start working after you have submitted the application for temporary protection to the police or to the border authorities.

## Work in Finland guide 

Check out the Work in Finland guide for the most important instructions from Finnish authorities in one place. 

## Leaving Finland 

If you are moving away from Finland, you must file a notification of move and take care of the related tax matters. 

This page is part of the European Commission’s Your Europe portal. Give the Commission feedback about this page.

You will automatically activate Suomi.fi Messages or electronic tax mail when you log in to MyTax.
